paragraphs.text: Family history is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance (e.g., affected sibs and/or parental consanguinity). Absence of a known family history does not preclude the diagnosis.

paragraphs.text: YIF1B -related neurodevelopmental disorder ( YIF1B -NDD) is characterized by severe-to-profound developmental delay / intellectual disability with variable motor abnormalities including axial hypotonia, peripheral hypertonia, dystonia, and dyskinesia; absence of speech in most individuals or very limited speech subject to regression; feeding difficulties; seizures; postnatal microcephaly with nonspecific brain MRI abnormalities; and ophthalmologic involvement (strabismus, nystagmus, optic atrophy, and cortical blindness). Some individuals have hypoventilation. To date, 25 individuals have been identified with biallelic pathogenic variants in YIF1B [ AlMuhaizea et al 2020 , Diaz et al 2020 , Medico Salsench et al 2021 , Sanri et al 2023 ]. The following description of the phenotypic features associated with this condition is based on these reports.
